title: Per-token tiling and sweep notes
content:
Purpose:
Short working notes describing an experiment sweep / heuristics doc for allocating reserved capacity in tiles (by region/model family/latency slice) and estimating per-token COGS for Hosted API. Intended as an input to the spreadsheet linked above and as a checklist of experiments for Optimize and Serving Runtime teams.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Idea: treat Dedicated/hosted capacity as discrete "tiles" sized by throughput and latency objective; map model-family x region x latency-tier to tile types.
- Use a small set of heuristics to pick tile sizes and batch policies, then simulate per-token COGS with KV cache and prefix reuse assumptions.
- Prioritized experiments: (1) batch scaling curves per model-family, (2) KV cache hit rate sensitivity, (3) quantization toggles (8-bit vs 4-bit) impact on throughput and accuracy.

Assumptions (base case used in the spreadsheet):
- Example hardware cost (amortized infra + infra ops): A100-equivalent $2.80 / hour; V100-equivalent $1.90 / hour used for smaller models.
- Baseline throughput (inference tokens/sec, steady-state, single replica):
  * small-llm-7B (q8): 950 tokens/s
  * small-llm-7B (q4): 1,400 tokens/s (higher throughput after quantization/optimizations)
  * med-llm-13B (q8): 420 tokens/s
  * large-llm-70B (q8): 90 tokens/s
- Average request length scenarios used: short (20 tokens), medium (120 tokens), long (800 tokens).
- KV/prefix cache: baseline hit rates: 0.12 global, 0.4 customer-specific hot prefixes, and a special-case 0.7 for assistant-style reuse (session pinned).
- Overhead adjustments: network + control-plane adds 8% to per-hour cost; misc ops 4% (total 12% uplift applied to raw infra).

Unit math examples (how the spreadsheet computes per-token COGS):
- tokens_per_hour = throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600
- adjusted_hourly_cost = gpu_hourly_cost * (1 + overhead_pct)
- per_token_raw = adjusted_hourly_cost / tokens_per_hour

Concrete example (small-llm-7B q8):
- throughput = 950 tokens/s -> tokens/hr = 950 * 3600 = 3,420,000
- gpu_hourly_cost = $2.80; overhead 12% -> adjusted = $3.136
- per_token_raw = 3.136 / 3,420,000 = $9.17e-7 (~0.000000917 USD/token)
- apply cache reuse effect: effective tokens_billed = tokens_served * (1 - cache_hit_rate * avg_prefix_reuse_fraction)
  * e.g., global cache hit 0.12 with reuse fraction 0.6 -> billed tokens factor = 1 - 0.12*0.6 = 0.928 -> effective per_billed_token = per_token_raw / 0.928 = $9.89e-7

Sensitivity snapshots we keep in the sheet (quick notes for readers):
- Throughput +/-15% moves per-token by roughly +/-15% linearly.
- GPU hourly +/-20% has direct proportional effect.
- Cache hit rate has diminishing returns after ~40% for most chat workloads because session-pinned reuse is limited.
- Quantization to q4: typical throughput uplift 35–60% depending on kernel maturity; however model-family accuracy/regression risk must be measured in eval harness before rollouts.

Tiling heuristic (working rules):
1) Tile definition: a tile is a bundle sized to serve N requests at p50 latency <= target, measured for a workload mix. Typical tile sizes: small tile (~1 replica of small-llm), medium tile (~2 replicas of med-llm), large tile (~1 replica of large-llm on beefier hw).
2) Map rules: choose tile by (peak RPS for workload slice, p50 latency target, tolerance for scaling jitter). Use historical 95th percentile traffic spikes to size tiles for critical customers.
3) Burst policy: allow 1.5x burst on each tile for short windows by borrowing across same-region tiles.
4) Autoscale thresholds: scale when sustained utilization > 60% for >= 5 minutes; downscale below 35% over 10 minutes.

Batching & latency heuristics used in sweep: 
- Auto-batcher targets a p50 latency budget (e.g., 120ms). If model can batch up to B tokens without violating the p50, pick B that maximizes tokens/sec per replica.
- For short requests (<50 tokens) prefer aggressive batching to reduce per-token cost; set max batching window to 20ms for p50-sensitive customers.
- For streaming-heavy clients, batch only within single-connection groups to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Recommended experiments (priority order):
1) Batch curve measurement across seq-lens (tooling ticket: JIRA-1284) — measure throughput vs p50 for each model-family and quantization profile. Output: curve to feed the tiling calculator. Owner: Ethan.
2) KV cache sensitivity matrix — vary hit rates 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and simulate per-token COGS for each region model pair. Owner: Priya.
3) Quantization safety ramp — A/B tests on a small set of customers with q4 encoding vs q8 to measure output quality regressions for 3 golden prompt sets. Owner: Applied ML.
4) Regional ratecard delta collection — confirm cloud instance pricing by region and update the spreadsheet inputs. Owner: Luca.

Prioritization notes / decision heuristics:
- If a change yields >8% per-token improvement at baseline traffic, it moves to high priority (possible knob: enable q4 + adjusted batch).
- If expected improvement <2% but high implementation risk, deprioritize.
- Prefer improvements that reduce marginal cost rather than fixed amortized cost when serving long tail customers.

Playbook / immediate actions (next 30 days):
- Wire batch-throughput curves into the tiling sheet (linked). Blocker: need real traces with service-level sampling. (Ticket created).
- Run cache-priming experiment for 3 top customers to measure customer-specific prefix reuse.
- Draft an internal one-pager for sales/solutions explaining how we can offer "tiling-optimized" reserved capacity plans (pricing/FAQ).

Risks and open questions (notes to revisit):
- Model regressions from quantization are non-linear with prompt type; need eval hooks that map to unit-econ delta.
- Cold-starts and model-switch fallbacks create transient token spikes; tiling needs guardrails to avoid transient overprovisioning.
- Multi-region replication and failover: do we double count reserved tiles for DR? Spreadsheet uses option flags: (a) active-active (double count), (b) active-passive (small standby), (c) cross-region failover (no double count) — need policy.

Owner & next steps:
- Owner: Maya Patel (product-optimize)
- Week 1: Ethan to submit batch curves + sample CSVs. Priya to run cache-sensitivity sim for baseline tile types.
- Week 2: Draft pricing impact memo for sales and add a sample pricing table in the spreadsheet (per-token vs per-request buckets).

Appendix: quick artifacts to copy into the spreadsheet when building scenarios:
- per_token_raw formula: "adjusted_hourly_cost / (throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600)"
- billed_token_factor = 1 - (cache_hit_rate * avg_reuse_fraction)
- final_per_billed_token = per_token_raw / billed_token_factor + per-request control-plane surcharge (if applied)
- example per-1000-token pricing sensitivity table (use spreadsheet to generate):
  * baseline small-llm (q8) -> ~$0.000917 per token -> $0.917 per 1000 tokens (before markup)
  * with q4 and batching improvements -> per token down to ~$0.00057 -> $0.57 per 1000 tokens

Notes-to-self style items (messy):
- Check regional power/cooling amortization for APAC — might nudge hourly down 3–5% in some regions.
- Explore a small POC of short-lived GPU pods sized for streaming-only workloads (could reduce per-token for tiny responses).
- Cross-check CPU pre/post processing costs for embedding-heavy routes (not included in first-pass tiling).

If you want I can push a trimmed "executive" view of the spreadsheet that shows three scenarios (conservative, base, aggressive) and a short policy recommendation for pricing and reserved-capacity packaging.

-- Maya
